questions.title: Testing Models and Controllers
questions.direct_answer: Model tests check rules in isolation: assert a validation (assert_not Post.new(title: '').save), a scope (assert_equal [p1,p2], Post.published), a method (assert_equal 80, post.excerpt.length). Controller tests (or request tests) check the HTTP layer: get '/posts/42'; assert_response :success; assert_equal 'My Post', response.body. In Rails 7, request tests (integration-style) are preferred over old controller tests — they hit the route, run the full stack, and check the response. Fixtures (test/fixtures/posts.yml) or factories seed test data. Run a single file with rails test test/models/post_test.rb; the whole suite with rails test.

sections.title: Model and controller tests
sections.content:
```ruby
# test/models/post_test.rb (MODEL: rules in isolation)
class PostTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test 'title is required' do
    p = Post.new(title: '')
    assert_not p.valid?               # validation
    assert p.errors[:title].any?
  end

  test 'published scope' do
    p1 = Post.create!(title: 'a', published_at: Time.current)
    p2 = Post.create!(title: 'b', published_at: nil)
    assert_includes Post.published, p1
    assert_not_includes Post.published, p2
  end
end

# test/controllers/posts_controller_test.rb (REQUEST: HTTP layer)
class PostsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test 'GET show returns the post' do
    post = Post.create!(title: 'My Post', body: 'x')
    get post_path(post)                  # hit the route (full stack)
    assert_response :success             # 200
    assert_includes response.body, 'My Post'
  end

  test 'POST create makes a post' do
    assert_difference('Post.count', 1) do
      post posts_path, params: { post: { title: 'New', body: 'y' } }
    end
    assert_response :redirect
  end
end
# Run one file:  rails test test/models/post_test.rb
# Run all:       rails test
```
